content:
The [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Baseball earned run average — earned runs per 9 innings pitched. Enter your earned runs allowed, complete innings pitched and outs in the partial inning and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Work out a baseball pitcher's earned run average (ERA): earned runs allowed per nine innings pitched. A pitcher who gives up 3 earned runs in 6 innings has an ERA of 4.50. Enter complete innings plus the outs in any partial inning — one out is a third of an inning, two outs are two thirds — because baseball counts innings in thirds, not tenths. Only earned runs count: runs that score because of errors or passed balls are excluded.

## How to use the ERA Calculator

Start by entering your earned runs allowed, then entering your complete innings pitched and finally choosing your outs in the partial inning from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the earned runs the pitcher allowed.
2. Enter the complete innings pitched.
3. Add the outs in the partial inning, if any — 1 out is a third of an inning.
4. Read the ERA: earned runs per nine innings.

## Formula

ERA = earned runs × 9 ÷ innings pitched. A partial inning counts as outs ÷ 3 — 1 out is ⅓ of an inning, 2 outs are ⅔.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 3 earned runs in 6 innings is an ERA of 4.50. The same 3 runs in 9 innings would be 3.00, and 3 runs in 6⅓ innings (6 innings plus 1 out) is 4.26. Try the same figures in the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Earned runs allowed: 3, Complete innings pitched: 6, Outs in the partial inning: 0 outs), the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) returns ERA: 4.5, Innings pitched: 6, Earned runs per inning: 0.5. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Batting Average Calculator](/batting-average-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Earned runs vs all runs

ERA only counts earned runs — runs that score without the help of an error or a passed ball. If a shortstop boots a grounder and the runner later scores, that run is unearned and does not touch the pitcher's ERA. The official scorer decides, which is why ERA can look unfair: a pitcher can allow no earned runs and still lose a game full of errors behind him.

## What is a good ERA?

In the modern game, an ERA under 3.00 is excellent, 3.00–4.00 is good, and the league average sits around 4.00–4.50 depending on the season. Before 1920, in the dead-ball era, ERAs under 2.00 were common; today, rule changes and better hitting have pushed the average up. Always compare a pitcher's ERA with the league average of the same season.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Count partial innings in thirds: 6.1 innings in a box score means 6⅓, not 6.1.
- ERA needs a decent sample — one bad outing can wreck a reliever's ERA for weeks.
- Compare ERAs within the same league and season: run environments change over time.

## Frequently asked questions

### How is ERA calculated?

Earned runs × 9 ÷ innings pitched. 3 earned runs in 6 innings is 3 × 9 ÷ 6 = 4.50. It is the number of earned runs the pitcher would allow over a full nine-inning game at the same rate. Try it with your own numbers in the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What does 6.2 innings pitched mean?

In baseball notation, 6.2 means 6 innings plus 2 outs — 6⅔ innings, not 6.2 decimal innings. The .1 is one third of an inning and .2 is two thirds. Try it with your own numbers in the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is a good ERA in baseball?

Under 3.00 is excellent, 3.00–4.00 is good, and around 4.00–4.50 is roughly league average in the modern game. Try it with your own numbers in the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the ERA Calculator use?

ERA = earned runs × 9 ÷ innings pitched. A partial inning counts as outs ÷ 3 — 1 out is ⅓ of an inning, 2 outs are ⅔. You can see it in action in the [ERA Calculator](/era-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
